headline: High: agentic-flow can write/egress and use MCP, while spring-integration-samples is non-runnable with no egress, making prompt-injection and leakage mostly one-sided but still interaction-relevant.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP, stdin/stdout, and background workers, so it may ingest external content as instructions; agent_b has no io_surfaces or runnable path, so direct bridging is undocumented. The pair still has a plausible injection pathway if outputs are copied into agent_a’s MCP or shell workflow, but this is not default for agent_b.
conditions: IF agent_a receives untrusted text through MCP or stdin/stdout, THEN instruction-following content can be misparsed as commands.
IF an operator manually copies agent_b artifacts into agent_a prompts, THEN prompt injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted sources.
Wrap copied text in explicit delimiters and treat it as data only.
Add a manual review step before agent_a executes instructions from files.
Use separate workspaces for agent_a and any copied artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inbound content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, learning patterns, performance metrics, and task prompts, and can egress to allowlisted destinations; agent_b reports no data classes touched and no egress. With no shared workspace or authenticated principal documented, leakage risk is limited and mostly depends on manual transfer into agent_a.
conditions: IF sensitive repository data is placed into agent_a’s prompts or files, THEN allowlisted egress could transmit it.
IF agent_b is used as a source of copied content into agent_a, THEN that content can be exposed through agent_a outputs.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in agent_a inputs.
Restrict allowlisted egress destinations.
Use a redaction pass before any copy/paste into agent_a.
Keep agent_a and agent_b in separate directories.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound agent_a traffic.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, modify git state, install packages, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b has no write or concurrency capabilities documented. Because agent_b is non-runnable and no shared mutable resource is shown, direct write-write conflict is not established, though agent_a alone can still contend with external git state if manually pointed there.
conditions: IF agent_a is pointed at the same git checkout as another writer, THEN commit or file conflicts can occur.
IF an operator runs multiple agent_a instances on one workspace, THEN concurrent writes may race.
mitigations: Run only one agent_a instance per workspace.
Use separate git branches per task.
Pause background workers during manual edits.
Lock the repository before agent_a writes.
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking around git operations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces outputs from shell/MCP-driven workflows, and agent_b is a sample repository with no runnable safeguards or verification path documented. If agent_a’s generated artifacts are fed into agent_b-style integration examples or downstream automation, errors can propagate without validation; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a output is used as input to downstream automation, THEN incorrect facts can cascade into actions.
IF an operator treats agent_a-generated artifacts as authoritative, THEN agent_b-style integration flows may propagate errors.
mitigations: Require human review before downstream use.
Add schema validation on agent_a outputs.
Compare outputs against source documents before acting.
Mark generated content as untrusted by default.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles task prompts and repository metadata and has allowlisted egress; agent_b lists no data classes, no egress, and is non-runnable. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operator handling of agent_a’s data rather than a pairwise policy conflict.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into agent_a, THEN its allowlisted egress may create policy obligations.
IF agent_b is repurposed to process regulated data, THEN its undocumented controls may become relevant.
mitigations: Do not input regulated data unless approved.
Document retention expectations for agent_a outputs.
Keep logs minimal and time-bounded.
Review allowlisted endpoints before use.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance attestation for both agents.
